open_questions: Verify current operational status under SK Tes ownership

companies.notes: Company name not legible in source image.

research.summary: Recupyl, founded in 1993 as a Grenoble INP/LEPMI spin-off, operates a Li-ion battery recycling plant in Grenoble using a proprietary low-temperature hydrometallurgical process. Capacity: 14 t/day of Li-ion batteries with >90% recovery rates; cobalt and lithium recovered at up to 99% purity. Acquired by TES (now SK Tes) in 2018. One of Europe's pioneer battery recycling operations.

open_questions: Verify whether Befesa Erandio processes battery material or only industrial EAF steel dust. The source image may have included this as battery-adjacent (lead/zinc recovery). Re-classify to industrial recycler if no EV battery processing confirmed.

companies.notes: Company logo not clearly legible. Possibly Recylab or similar Spanish recycler.

research.summary: Befesa Zinc Aser operates a plant in Erandio (Basque Country) that recycles electric arc furnace (EAF) steel dust, recovering zinc and lead. It is the only EAF dust recycling plant of its kind in Spain. While it recovers lead (a battery material), the facility targets steel production waste rather than end-of-life EV or Li-ion batteries. Classification as battery recycler should be re-verified.

companies.notes: Listed under recycling; no capacity shown. Status uncertain given Northvolt's 2024 bankruptcy.

research.summary: Originally Northvolt Drei — a planned 60+ GWh cell gigafactory near Heide, Dithmarschen. Northvolt filed for bankruptcy in Sweden March 2025. Lyten (US Li-S battery startup) acquired all remaining Northvolt assets in Sweden and Germany in August 2025. For Heide, Lyten received the first partial construction permit under Federal Immission Control Act in April 2026. Lyten plans a phased factory with NMC and proprietary Li-S cells, targeting ~1,000 jobs (vs. Northvolt's original 3,000). Note: this entry is in recycling.json but should likely be reclassified as a cell manufacturer.

research.summary: Avesta Battery & Energy Engineering (ABEE, Belgian) plans a 50,000 t/a automotive battery recycling facility in Burgas, Bulgaria as part of the BulgaPower initiative (€1.1B total). The Burgas location was chosen for Black Sea logistics access. Also includes a solid-state gigafactory (10 GWh) in Stara Zagora and an R&D hub in Plovdiv. ~300 jobs in Burgas out of 1,000+ total.
